title: Asymmetric token floor prototype with streaming soft-commit and SQ gap analysis
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current single-axis per-token billing conflates ingress (input) and egress (output) costs for streaming and non-streaming requests. Customers with prefix-heavy workloads or high short-stream frequency see surprising bills or are forced to overcommit. Enterprise customers have asked for clearer contract language in the security questionnaire (SQ) about how streaming sessions and partial responses are billed and audited.

Proposal: Run a 6-week prototype that decouples ingress and egress metering for hosted API calls and introduces a streaming soft-commit floor. Key elements: (1) Split per-token rates into input_token_rate and output_token_rate (configurable per-catalog model). (2) Streaming soft-commit: apply a small per-stream minimum (expressed in tokens) with a configurable grace credit window for bursts to avoid penalizing short-lived interactive sessions. (3) Add explicit invoice fields and audit log events to satisfy SQ requirements: stream_id, effective_input_tokens, effective_output_tokens, soft_commit_applied, and grace_credit_used.

Why now: Several enterprise RFPs flagged streaming ambiguity in the SQ, and pricing simulations show this model reduces sticker shock for latency-sensitive UIs while preserving unit economics for batch/LLM-compute-heavy workloads.

Hypothesis: Introducing directional rates + a low streaming floor (e.g., 8 tokens) with a 72-hour grace credit pool increases paid commits by ~4–9% from mid-market customers and reduces support billing disputes by ~30% for customers with high short-session ratios.
acceptance_criteria: Analytics pipeline emits directionally split token counts per request (input_tokens, output_tokens, stream_id)
Billing prototype charges using configurable input/output rates and applies per-stream soft-commit floor
Console shows per-route ingress/egress token breakdown and highlights streams where grace credits were used
SQ docs updated with billing-as-audit entries and sample invoice line items; legal and security sign-off obtained
Simulations prove no >10% downside to unit margin across sampled model workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings)
success_metrics: Revenue delta: +4% to +9% for targeted cohorts over 6 weeks
Support disputes about unexpected streaming charges: -30% for pilot accounts
Enterprise conversion uplift where SQ clarity was blocker: +12% in pilot segment
Console adoption: 65% of pilot users view ingress/egress breakdown within first 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (week 0-1): implement telemetry and simulator; create config knobs for per-model input/output rates. Phase 1 (week 2-3): internal dogfood with Redwood apps and 5 pilot customers; enable soft-commit = 8 tokens, grace pool 72h, default input_rate = 0.5 * output_rate. Phase 2 (week 4-5): iterate on rates from telemetry, add invoice fields, run legal/SQ review. Phase 3 (week 6): open opt-in pilot for broader PLG users and prepare migration docs + SDK changes. Finalize contract language for Reserved Capacity and Enterprise SQ addendum before GA.
notes: Engineering: need to ensure streaming sessions get deterministic stream_id and that prefix caching doesn't double-count input tokens when cache hits occur
Billing: per-stream floor introduces potential rounding edge cases for micro-billed streams; agree to round up to nearest token and log raw fractional token-decisions in audits
Product: default rates must be conservative to avoid unit-margin erosion; propose initial input_rate = 0.45 * output_rate for chat models and 0.15 * output_rate for embeddings ingestion
Design: Console invoice UX needs a per-invoice expandable section for stream-level line items; consider sampling display for invoices exceeding 1000 streams
Legal/Security: SQ wants cryptographic proof-of-billing events; propose signed logfile export (S3 + customer KMS) for enterprise customers
